doc.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]

title: Johnny Frigo and The Toulouse in Chicago
summary: Budd met Frigo at a Gibson party and now visits his weekly gig in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Did you ever interview — I think I saw your list — you did interview Johnny Fregal maybe, did you?
Do you know who he is at all?

I met him purely by chance too at one of the Gibson parties. I was wandering around looking for musicians to talk to, so my wife was minding her business and sat in the chair. And it was the empty chair beside her and Johnny Fregal came around and said “is this an empty seat, my wife is looking for a seat, could she sit with you?” And she said “yes, certainly she can.” And so then when I came back, whatever, she said “this is the wife of that Johnny Fregal that you saw” and I admired him because he played like Joe Venuti. And so I met him at that time and he became interested and he said “I live in Chicago, and I play one night a week at a place called The Toulouse Restaurant. And the rest of the week I do commercials and I also paint.” He’s a great artist and poet and so forth. He said “If you come to Chicago come and see me.” So I’ve been making a habit of going to Chicago maybe once a year, and on Monday or Tuesday are the only nights he plays, I go out to Toulouse and see him, and he always has me play one tune and makes a big fuss about it. Most of the people there, it’s a small room, it’s about as big as this suite that you’re in here. And a lot of them are people from the Chicago Symphony, musicians. They’re real listeners. And he’s in their league. And they make a big fuss that this doctor © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -20-
plays so good. It’s not. It’s like a plumber taking out your appendix again. But Fregel’s been a wonderful person.
